RdistNN

RdistNN implements distributional nearest-neighbor (DNN) localization for local conditional moment and Z-estimation problems. The pre-public interface overhaul is implemented; the package now uses consistent estimator, tuning, diagnostic, plotting, and simulation contracts across its primary workflows.

  • Core distance/rank/weight primitives (weights_dnn(), weights_matrix(), custom registries)
  • User-level wrappers for localized estimation: np_dnn(), cate_dnn(), and plqr_dnn()
  • Unified diagnostics for fitted local estimators via diagnostics()
  • Built-in post-estimation methods (summary(), confint(), predict())
  • Tuning-grid inspection through candidate_fit(), candidate_fits(), and plot_tuning()
  • ggplot2 postestimation views for estimates, overlap, weights, influence, conditioning, calibration, and dashboards
  • Fast delete-1 jackknife options (jackknife = "fast" and "loo") for standard errors
  • Simulation infrastructure for the paper’s CATE study: sim_cate_data(), sim_cate_one_rep(), sim_cate_run(), summarise_sim_results()
  • Experimental companion functionality: local IV-GMM wrappers and simulation helpers (gmm_model_dr_iv(), gmm_dnn(), sim_iv_data(), sim_iv_run(), iv_demo_data()) are included for ongoing companion-paper development; their API and theorem alignment may change before the GMM paper is released

Status: active research package. APIs may continue to evolve.

This package accompanies Orthogonal Inference for Conditional Z-Estimation without Cross-Fitting.

API tiers

Not all exported functions carry the same stability promise:

Tier Meaning Examples Public docs
Stable user API expected to survive the public release weights_dnn(), np_dnn(), cate_dnn(), plqr_dnn(), fitted-object methods, diagnostics, tuning, and plotting helpers README + main reference groups
Developer API extension points for custom components distance / rank-weight / score specs and registries “Developer API” reference groups
Paper replication API tied to the paper’s simulation study sim_cate_*, summarise_sim_results() replication reference group + vignette
Experimental companion API may change before the companion papers are released gmm_dnn(), sim_iv_*, TDNN/jackknife infrastructure “Experimental”/“Advanced” reference groups
Internal not exported low-level distance/order/rank-table plumbing none

For exact DNN weights, the package works with the full rank permutation at each target. Exact single-scale DNN has finite-population support through rank n - s + k; in the paper-default k = 1 case this is n - s + 1. Thus s is a subsample/localization order, not an s-nearest-neighbor truncation. The optional neighbors extra reports the first k nearest observations used inside each size-s subsample, not the full DNN weight support. The implementation also supports fixed top-k DNN kernels. Extending the fixed-k theory from the 1-NN derivation is essentially direct, but the current accompanying manuscript derivations are written for k = 1; use larger fixed k values as implementation-supported generalizations until that proof text is added.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("JakobJuergens/RdistNN")

Platform compatibility

R package binaries install without a local compiler when a matching binary is available. Installation from source requires a working C++17 toolchain and Rcpp on Windows, macOS, and Linux. OpenMP is optional: the package uses R’s portable SHLIB_OPENMP_CXXFLAGS, so compiled kernels run serially on toolchains where R does not provide OpenMP flags.

The package includes R implementations for supported distance, score, and jackknife operations and uses them when the corresponding compiled fast path is unavailable at runtime. Set options(RdistNN.use_compiled = FALSE) to force those R paths for reproducibility or diagnosis; CI checks compiled/fallback parity on every supported platform. Those algorithmic fallbacks do not turn the package into a no-compiler source package: the package itself contains registered C++ code and must still be compiled when installed from source.

The full GitHub Actions release matrix covers Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64, macOS arm64, and macOS x86-64, plus R release, devel, and oldrel on Linux. Pull requests, pushes to the default branch, and manual runs all execute the full matrix so platform regressions are blocked before merge.

Quick Start

1) DNN Weights and Local Means (np_dnn) 

library(RdistNN)

set.seed(1)
demo_np <- np_demo_data(n = 250, p = 2, design = "sinusoidal", seed = 1)

fit_np <- np_dnn(
  data = demo_np$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  x0 = c(0, 0),
  distance = "l2",
  method = "exact",
  # Toy choice for a tiny example; use tuning_dnn_paper() in paper-style runs.
  k = 1L, s = 3L,
  se = TRUE,
  jackknife = "fast",
  return = c("W", "ess", "neighbors")
)

fit_np$mu
fit_np$se
diagnostics(fit_np)

2) CATE Estimation (cate_dnn) and Methods 

library(RdistNN)

demo_cate <- cate_demo_data(n = 300, p = 2, design = "hetero", seed = 1)
df <- demo_cate$data
df$m1_oracle <- df$m0_oracle + df$tau_oracle

fit_cate <- cate_dnn(
  data = df,
  x0 = rep(0, 2),
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  t_col = "D",
  m0_col = "m0_oracle",
  m1_col = "m1_oracle",
  e_col = "e_oracle",
  distance = "l2",
  method = "exact",
  # Toy choice for a tiny example; use tuning_dnn_paper() in paper-style runs.
  k = 1L, s = 3L,
  se = TRUE,
  jackknife = "fast",
  return = c("W", "psi", "nuisance")
)

summary(fit_cate)
confint(fit_cate)
diagnostics(fit_cate)
predict(fit_cate, x0 = c(0.2, -0.1), interval = "confidence")

CATE inference contract

Neyman orthogonality controls first-order population nuisance drift. It does not, by itself, validate arbitrary nuisance predictions estimated on the same observations used by cate_dnn(). Valid full-sample reuse additionally requires the nuisance-rate and full-state stability conditions in the paper. cate_dnn() computes the estimator and requested jackknife procedure but cannot diagnose whether an arbitrary learner satisfies those conditions. Supported inputs include oracle quantities, cross-fitted or out-of-fold predictions, and full-sample predictions from learners for which the paper’s rate and stability conditions are credible.

3) Local PLQR Orthogonal Moments (plqr_dnn)

PLQR support currently evaluates localized orthogonal PLQR moments and direct-sandwich coefficient uncertainty at supplied coefficient values. Local root-solving for target-specific PLQR coefficients is under development. Coefficient-level standard errors and confidence intervals require threshold-density values via density / density_col.

library(RdistNN)

demo_plqr <- plqr_demo_data(n = 250, p = 2, p_d = 2, tau = 0.5, seed = 1)
# demo_plqr$data already includes density_oracle, the true (constant)
# conditional density of Y at the quantile threshold for the demo DGP.

fit_plqr <- plqr_dnn(
  data = demo_plqr$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  D_cols = c("D1", "D2"),
  g_col = "g_oracle",
  mD_cols = c("mD1", "mD2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  density_col = "density_oracle",
  theta_eval = demo_plqr$truth$theta_true,
  tau = 0.5,
  x0 = c(0, 0),
  distance = "l2",
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  tuning = tuning_dnn_paper(),
  se = TRUE,
  return = c("W", "score", "ess")
)

summary(fit_plqr)
confint(fit_plqr)
predict(fit_plqr, x0 = c(0.25, -0.25), interval = "confidence")
diagnostics(fit_plqr)

tuning_dnn_paper() uses the paper’s finite-sample default lambda = 0.4 and sensitivity grid c(0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.75), with s(lambda) = floor(lambda * n^((kx + 1)/(kx + 2))). Explicit lambda, lambda_grid, fixed s, and custom tuning specifications remain supported; lambda = 1 is a more aggressive localization benchmark.

Without a density input, plqr_dnn() still evaluates the localized moment and reports moment_se, a jackknife moment diagnostic; that is not coefficient-level inference.

4) CATE Simulation Study 

library(RdistNN)

# Draw one dataset from a named DGP (oracle AIPW and nuisance columns included)
dgp <- sim_cate_data("dgp2_nonlinear", n = 300, kx = 2, seed = 1)
dgp$tau_x0   # true CATE at the default x0 = (1, 0)

# Run one replicate and get bias / SE / coverage metrics
r <- sim_cate_one_rep(n = 300, kx = 2, k = 1, s = 12,
                      design = "dgp2_nonlinear", seed = 1)
r

# Small Monte Carlo grid (use n_reps = 500 for paper results)
raw <- sim_cate_run(
  designs = c("dgp1_linear", "dgp2_nonlinear"),
  n_vals  = 300L,
  n_reps  = 5L,
  verbose = FALSE
)
summarise_sim_results(raw)

For DNN and local-constant rows, the raw and summary outputs also expose the realized DNN-weighted truth, realized localization drift, estimator remainder, physical neighborhood radius, arm-specific effective sample sizes, and studentized finite-sample shape. The weighted truth sum_i W_i,s(x0) tau_0(X_i) is random and is not the deterministic population branch alpha_s(x0). With x0 and (n, s) fixed, expectation over the i.i.d. covariate sample and complete-DNN exchangeability give E[sum_i W_i,s(x0) tau_0(X_i)] = alpha_s(x0). The estimator remainder combines centered score variation with fitted-state effects; paired feasible/oracle comparisons isolate the latter. These fields keep localization, score variation, and nuisance fitting distinct instead of treating coverage as a single undifferentiated diagnostic.

5) Local IV-GMM (experimental)

Experimental local IV-GMM wrappers (gmm_model_dr_iv(), gmm_dnn()) and simulation helpers (sim_iv_*, iv_demo_data()) are included for companion-paper development. Their API may change before the GMM paper is released. See vignette("local-iv-estimation", package = "RdistNN") for the full workflow.

6) Custom Distances, Rank Weights, and Scores 

library(RdistNN)

register_distance("linf_demo", function(X, x0, ctx = NULL) {
  apply(abs(X - matrix(x0, nrow(X), ncol(X), byrow = TRUE)), 1L, max)
})

register_rank_weight("inv_rank_demo", function(ranks) {
  w <- 1 / as.numeric(ranks)
  w / sum(w)
})

X <- as.matrix(np_demo_data(n = 80, p = 2, seed = 1)$data[, c("X1", "X2")])
W <- weights_matrix(
  X = X,
  x0 = c(0, 0),
  ranking = "linf_demo",
  weight = get_rank_weight("inv_rank_demo"),
  return = "W"
)$W
dim(W)

sc_affine <- new_score(
  name = "affine_order1",
  order = 1L,
  eval_param = function(idxs, data, theta, ctx, rng = NULL) {
    theta[1] * data$Y[idxs] + theta[2]
  }
)

path <- score_diff_path(sc_affine, data = data.frame(Y = c(1, 2, 4)), method = "fd")
path$grad(2L, theta = c(0.5, 1))

The full extension guide is vignette("extending", package = "RdistNN"). It covers setup() / eval_batch() patterns, custom ranking inputs to weights_matrix(), parameter-aware scores, and debugging with return = c("dx", "ord", "ranks").

Visualisation

Fitted objects have ggplot2-based plot()/autoplot() methods (ggplot2 is a suggested dependency). The flagship view is the CATE profile: point estimates with jackknife confidence bounds along a covariate profile, a zero reference line, and an honesty caption reporting the effective local sample size and the kernel-order provenance.

library(RdistNN)

set.seed(42)
n <- 1000
X <- cbind(X1 = runif(n, -2, 2), X2 = rnorm(n))
e <- plogis(0.4 * X[, "X1"])                    # oracle propensity
tau <- 1 + sin(X[, "X1"])                       # true CATE along X1
m0 <- X[, "X1"] - 0.5 * X[, "X2"]               # oracle control mean
treat <- as.integer(runif(n) < e)
Y <- m0 + treat * tau + rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)

df <- data.frame(X, T = treat, Y = Y, e = e, m0 = m0, m1 = m0 + tau)
X0 <- cbind(X1 = seq(-1.8, 1.8, length.out = 21), X2 = 0)

fit <- cate_dnn(
  data = df, x_cols = c("X1", "X2"), y_col = "Y", t_col = "T",
  e_col = "e", m0_col = "m0", m1_col = "m1",
  X0 = X0, k = 1L, se = TRUE, jackknife = "fast"
)

plot(fit)

The plotting surface mirrors the fitted-object diagnostic contract: plot_estimates() handles coefficient profiles and intervals, plot_overlap() shows local treatment and propensity support, plot_influence() identifies high-contribution observations, plot_tuning() compares feasible tuning candidates, and plot_dashboard() assembles the main review panels. plot_conditioning() and plot_calibration() provide specialized PLQR/GMM views.

Weight-geometry views show what the estimator averaged over: plot_weights(fit, type = "kernel") draws the effective data-driven kernel (weight against distance), type = "profile" the decay by rank, and type = "cumulative" the concentration of the weight mass. All panels are regular ggplot objects and can be re-themed or extended with + as usual; plot_data_estimates(), plot_data_weights(), and plot_data_diagnostics() expose the underlying tidy frames for custom figures.

Development Notes

  • Engine selection is automatic: compiled code is used when available, otherwise robust R fallbacks are used.
  • Deterministic tie handling is built in for reproducibility.
  • Tests use testthat (edition 3). Run devtools::test() for the suite and devtools::check() for the release gate.
  • The remaining pre-public documentation item is a dedicated notation and package-conventions article; the general conditional-Z front end and package-level SIPP workflow are longer-term work.
  • Rebuild this README from source with devtools::build_readme().
